title: PCIe Fault Hot-Replace and Warm Backfill (WIP)
content:
Summary:
This is a working runbook for handling PCIe fabric-related GPU failures that require a hot-replace of the accelerator module and a warm backfill of capacity into the serving cluster. Focused on cloud/on-prem nodes with NVLink/NVSwitch topologies where a PCIe error cascade can cause degraded throughput across many pods.

Intended audience:
- Oncall SREs
- Field engineers doing physical swaps
- Release engineers coordinating capacity adjustments

When to use this document (high level):
- Node shows repeated PCIe AER errors in dmesg/syslog and kernel reports device reset loops (sometimes shows as MULTIPLE GPU resets within an hour).
- SMART/telemetry indicates PCIe endpoint errors or link training failures rather than pure GPU memory ECC faults.
- Remote soft-restart attempts (drivers, container restarts) do not remove the resets and pod-level evictions continue for the same node.

Quick triage (first 15 minutes):
- Check incidents dashboard and alerts: prometheus -> rate(gpu_reset_total[5m]) > 0 across nodes?
- Query node logs: sudo journalctl -k | tail -n 200 | grep -i "AER\|pcie\|reset"
- Check kernel oops messages for IOMMU faults.
- If GPU is detected but flapping: mark node as candidate for hot-replace.

Immediate mitigation (safety-first):
1) Route new traffic away: cordon the node ASAP to avoid new pods scheduling.
  - kubectl cordon <node-name>
2) Graceful drain for existing pods with priority fallback:
  - kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60 --timeout=10m
  - Notes: for critical latency paths, use --pod-selector to keep only critical pods (manual judgement).
3) If draining hangs due to long-running workloads, escalate to platform-lead and consider workload-level fallback (route traffic to dedicated pool).

Hardware/Field steps (coordinated with Field Eng / HW team):
Preconditions: Ensure you have physical access or remote BMC/IPMI credentials, spare GPU module in approved cabinet, ESD precautions, and change-window approval if required.
1) BMC access and health checks:
  - ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc-ip> -U <user> -P <pass> chassis status
  - Check SEL: ipmitool sel list | tail -n 50 for PCIe errors or thermal events.
2) Soft power-cycle node via BMC if node is still responsive: ipmitool chassis power cycle
  - Wait 10 minutes, re-check dmesg for AER counts.
  - If resets persist after power cycle -> proceed to physical hot-replace.
3) Confirm physical slot and label mapping (IMPORTANT):
  - Use rack asset spreadsheet (ask lin/infra-owner) to map server serial -> slot -> GPU label. Avoid assumptions; double-check sticker.
4) Hot-extract procedure (field eng):
  - Put node into maintenance mode (physically place a maintenance tag).
  - Remove PCIe retention screws and extract the accelerator following vendor guide (keep static wrist strap).
  - Inspect riser / connectors for debris, bent pins, or burn marks. Photograph any anomaly.
  - Replace with qualified spare (ensure firmware/board match).
5) Re-seat, secure, and power on node via BMC.
  - Monitor BMC logs for link training.
  - On boot, run vendor diagnostics (e.g., nvidia-smi -q, vendor diag package).

Software/Node recovery steps post-replace:
1) Confirm node health in k8s: kubectl get nodes | grep <node-name>
2) Remove taints or maintenance labels applied earlier.
3) Rejoin node to pool: ensure kubelet version & kube-proxy are running.
4) Run quick smoke: run a small batch of inference containers pinned to node (use test image) to validate GPU stability for 30–45m.
5) Check Prometheus for metrics:
  - grafana query examples: rate(gpu_reset_total[5m]), node_cpu_seconds_total, gpu_temperature_celsius{job="nvidia"}
  - Ensure no rising error counters for PCIe or GPU reset.

Warm backfill and capacity injection (controlled):
- Strategy: add capacity incrementally from spare node pool so autoscaling/routing doesn't get overwhelmed.
Steps:
1) Add 10–20% of capacity for the affected node's shard to the scheduler (create nodepool label or scale-up N nodes if autoscaler managed).
2) Enable traffic to new nodes via routing policy (Console route: region -> dedicated-pool).
3) Observe latency and error budgets for 15–30m. If stable, increment to 50% then full.
4) If errors reappear, cordon new nodes and rollback to previous routing policy.

Acceptance criteria for returning node to full production:
- 2 hours without any PCIe/gpu reset metrics > baseline across 5m windows.
- No kernel oops or IOMMU faults in the last 120 minutes.
- Smoke inference load at 25% of expected peak for 1 hour without errors or tail latency regressions.
- All dependent services show SLOs within 2% of normal for the test window.

Rollback plan (if replaced GPU shows regressions):
- If hardware fails diagnostics or early smoke tests: re-seat original module (if previously tested) or move traffic to spare pool and schedule full node rebuild (reimage).
- If multiple nodes show the same failure pattern after replacement, escalate to infra-ops: suspect riser/backplane or switch-level problem.

Observability queries / quick checks (examples to paste into Grafana/Prometheus):
- PromQL: increase(gpu_reset_total[1h]) > 0
- PromQL: rate(node_pci_errors_total[5m]) > 0
- Logs: kubectl -n kube-system logs -l k8s-app=kubelet --since=1h | grep -i pcie
- BMC SEL: ipmitool sel list | grep -i pcie

Communications play (who to ping):
- Pager duty: SRE-oncall (primary) -> if hardware: page Field-Eng (oncall) -> infra-owner/managers
- Slack: #sre-oncall, #field-eng, #infra-hardware (post updates every 15 min during active replace)
- Customer comms: status once node drained and replacement in progress, update if ETA to return > 2 hours.

Post-incident analysis items (to capture during and after event):
- Exact kernel messages and timestamps for first PCIe AER count.
- Which riser / slot showed the fault.
- Spare serial used and firmware version (keep in HW inventory).
- Time-to-backfill and time-to-recover metrics (for SLO reporting).

Known gotchas and notes-to-self (informal):
- Some vendor GPUs will report successful boot but still flake with link training errors after load — a 30–45m soak under load is essential.
- Replacing GPU without checking riser firmware has bitten us before. Add riser firmware check to preflight.
- On some Dell chassis, the carrier board will show signs of wear on the retainer clip; if repeated failures in same rack, escalate for rack-level inspection.
- If node was running Dedicated workloads with pinned volumes, draining might fail due to storage locks — coordinate with infra-storage to temporarily detach.

TODOs (shelf items to make runbook less manual):
- Add automation script to map BMC IP -> rack -> slot (blocked on asset-tagging cleanup).
- Small Playbook: automated K8s cordon/drain + toggle route policy script (ops-scripts PR 127 pending review).
- Add a short run of vendor riser firmware check to the standard node health check.

Postmortem checklist (post recover):
- Create incident timeline and attach photos of physical damage to Jira-SRE-3192.
- Update HW inventory with spare serial / firmware.
- Schedule rack-level inspection if >1 failure in same rack within 30 days.
- Review whether warm backfill timing was optimal (did we under/over-inject?)

Appendix: Useful commands and quick copy-paste
- kubectl cordon <node-name>
- kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60 --timeout=10m
- ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc-ip> -U <user> -P <pass> sel elist | tail -n 50
- journalctl -k | grep -i pcie | tail -n 200
- nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE

Contact list (for handoffs):
- Field engineering oncall: Marco Ruiz
- Hardware inventory owner: Lina Chen
- Platform lead for capacity: Devon O'Neill

End notes:
This is intentionally a terse working draft. Need to convert to a shorter cheatsheet for pagers and a companion checklist for field engineers (photos and exact screw torque specs).

Last edits: 2025-01-12 by Aisha (added warm backfill steps + observability queries)
